title: What If Krakatoa Erupted Like It Did in 1883?

scenes.text: What if Krakatoa erupted again? The loudest sound ever recorded was not the scariest part.
In 1883 the blast was heard almost five thousand kilometers away, and the pressure wave circled the planet several times.
The ash cloud rose around twenty-seven kilometers into the sky.
Tsunamis up to roughly thirty meters tall hit nearby islands. More than thirty-six thousand people died, mostly from the waves.
Ash and gas hung in the upper atmosphere. Northern Hemisphere summer cooled by about half a degree the next year.
Sunsets burned red for years. Artists sketched thousands of them. One mountain in Indonesia, and the whole world watched the sky.

description:
What if Krakatoa erupted again, like in 1883?
The blast was heard nearly 5,000 km away, tsunamis killed more than 36,000 people, and sunsets turned red worldwide.
